owner_referrals.proposed_local_argument: For atoms a=(a_i), b=(b_i), W1(N^-1 sum delta_(a_i),nu) differs from W1(N^-1 sum delta_(b_i),nu) by at most N^-1 sum d_Z(a_i,b_i): split any coupling equally among repeated labels at the same atom and transfer each labeled mass from a_i to b_i; use the triangle inequality and then take infima, in both directions. Thus the empirical cost at a fixed time is continuous in its finitely many atoms and measurable in the iid coordinates. On a compact initial-support finite-time slab, bounded acceleration bounds velocities uniformly; the deterministic characteristic flow and particle flow give uniform continuity in time of both coupling costs, by transporting any coupling between neighboring times. The supremum over [-T,T] equals a supremum over a fixed countable dense set of times, and is therefore measurable. This is a proof-only addition and does not change a public interface.
